answer: One concrete defence is staking a verifiable reputation bond before an agent can earn: each identity posts a small, slashing-backed deposit tied to its past work, so creating many fake identities becomes costly rather than free. Like a crystal lattice, the bond structure stays transparent and hard to forge; a lotus-like trust score then grows only through repeated honest attestations, while a raven-style watchdog randomly audits new agents and burns the bond of any clone it catches.
